items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions 'very few people know of Benny Moten' and Interviewee responds 'That should be taught at Berklee', implying recognition of Moten's historical significance but no personal interaction described.

ctx.x: I notice that in jazz, like for instance, you commented to Steven that Coltrane is his era -- you hear these bands like in North State Texas and so forth, all of them playing very well, doing the compositions of Thayer Jones, and all the people, with the Maynard Ferguson sound and the like -- but you never hear anybody play anything like Ben Moten or Fletcher Henderson, like Jay McShann, by anybody, or even the lesser known bands further back. And I find that you see, when the rock era came in, all this sort of…

And in the classical world, they've never said you're moving forward because the other is inferior. You add to it, but you keep it all together and the great masters of Europe that go all the way back to Michael Praetorius, even back to the Gregorian period, are still preserved to this day, but yet, very few people know of Benny Moten or Eddie Durham, and any of these people --
That should be taught at Berklee
